video.title: View Model, Observable & Bindable | Day 139
video.description:
Learn to explain how a SwiftUI screen uses a model class: View Model, Observable & Bindable, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
View Model - A class that holds the data and the logic for one screen.
Observable - A macro that makes a class tell SwiftUI when its properties change.
Bindable - A property wrapper that creates bindings to the properties of a model that you pass in.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain View Model, Observable and Bindable in English?

dialogue.title: Move data into a model

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I moved my note data into a class named `Note`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Many teams call that a View Model, a class that holds the data and the logic for a screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How does SwiftUI know when `Note` changes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mark the class as Observable. Then SwiftUI redraws any view that reads its properties.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I forgot the Observable macro at first, and the screen never updated.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, without Observable the View Model is only a plain class.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now the text field needs `$note.title`, but I get an error.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add Bindable to the property. Bindable creates bindings to the properties of an Observable model.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. State is for values the view owns. Bindable is for a model that you pass in.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Should every screen have its own View Model?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not always. Use one when the screen has real logic. Otherwise State is enough.
Put the screen logic in a View Model.
